text:
Interviewed the stakeholder brief against the intent template, one section at a time, and answered only what the brief itself says. The brief describes a permit intake workflow: applicants currently submit paper forms that a clerk re-keys by hand, which is slow and error-prone, and the brief asks for an online form that lets an applicant submit and track a permit application without a clerk re-entering it.

Wrote intent/permit-intake.md from the template. Problem, proposed outcome, affected users and systems, and constraints all came straight from the brief. The brief does not say how many applications the office handles today or what "track" should mean beyond submission, so both are recorded under Open questions rather than assumed. The brief did not define any term missing from constitution.md's J4 table, so that table is unchanged.

Touched nothing outside intent/permit-intake.md; the brief itself was read, not edited.

files.intent/permit-intake.md:
# Intent: Permit intake
Status: draft

## Problem
Applicants submit permit applications on paper. A clerk re-keys each one into the case system by hand, which is slow and introduces transcription errors.

## Proposed outcome
An applicant can submit a permit application online and it reaches the case system without a clerk re-keying it.

## Affected users and systems
- Applicants, who currently submit paper forms.
- Intake clerks, who currently re-key submissions.
- The case system that applications land in today.

## Constraints
- Must integrate with the existing case system; the brief does not say which one.

## Evidence
Observations that motivated this intent. Link criterion IDs (@R-xx.y) when known.
- The brief states re-keying is slow and error-prone; it gives no volume or error-rate figures.

## Open questions
- [ ] How many permit applications does the office handle per week or month today?
- [ ] What does "track" an application mean beyond initial submission — status only, or a full history?
- [ ] Which case system must the new intake reach, and does it expose an API today?
